Maya Li: quick flag 1622 16issue after our latest int8->int4 quant run: canaries show higher failure rate on short prompts (under 40 tokens). label queue has ballooned. anyone free to triage? :wave:
Priya Singh: whats the failure signal? are labels rejecting for quality or is it dedupe noise?
Evan R: from the canary logs it looks like both. lots of near-duplicates that never made it into golden, and some model regressions where answers truncate or hallucinate on terse inputs.
Omar Patel: sounds like the ingest dedupe is too late. we sample then dedupe; bad for labelers. idea: run a lightweight prefilter at ingest to knock out obvious exact/near dupes. keep paraphrase candidates for manual review.
Maya Li: agree. two-stage prefilter: 1) normalized exact hash drop 2) inexpensive ngram-jaccard or fast sim to flag. prefer flagging vs dropping for anything "close".
Priya Singh: propose thresholds: exact md5 after normalization -> drop. ngram-jaccard >= 0.88 -> flag. embed-sim >= 0.90 -> flag for label ops if ngram < 0.88.
Evan R: that seems conservative enough to avoid losing paraphrases. can LabelBot run a dry-run on the last 10k ingests and give counts? also include breakdown by prompt length and by model failure label.
LabelBot: starting job dryrun-176119-fasterprefilter on ingest-window=10k. will return counts summary to thread when complete.
Maya Li: also FYI: if dry-run shows >35% save on label effort we should bump label batch size and schedule a micro-golden refresh to reduce anchor gaps created by quant shift.
-- 8 minutes later --
LabelBot: dryrun complete. ingest=10,034 items. exact-normalized-hash-dropped=3,782. ngram-flagged=1,246. embed-flagged=978 (overlap w/ ngram=412). remaining-for-labeling=4,468. dedupe drop ~= 37.7%. short-prompt (<=40 tokens) fraction of remaining=62%. I attached CSV to job artifact: s3://label-dryruns/dryrun-176119-2026-03-22.csv
Priya Singh: nice. 37.7% reduction is in line with expectations. label ops capacity increase request: can we push +25% batch size for next 3 waves to burn down backlog?
Omar Patel: yes, but we should gate it on the micro-golden being ready. I can assemble candidate micro-golden list from high-value fallbacks and safety cases.
Evan R: PR plan: Ill open prefilter PR `prefilter/fast-dedupe-176119` with a config toggle (dry_run=true), parameters for md5 norm, ngram_k=3, jaccard_thresh=0.88, embed_thresh=0.90. will include metrics hooks.
Maya Li: can you include a small python snippet in the PR for the normalization + md5? saves copy/paste for labelops.
Evan R: sure. snippet below:
```python
# normalize and fingerprint
import hashlib, re
def norm_fp(text):
    t = text.lower()
    t = re.sub(r"[\\p{Punct}]", "", t)
    t = re.sub(r"\\s+", " ", t).strip()
    return hashlib.md5(t.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
```
Priya Singh: SGTM. timeline: Omar will hand off micro-golden candidates by Monday noon; label ops says they can take a +25% wave starting Wednesday. Evan aim to have draft PR by EOD Tuesday so we can flip toggle mid-week if metrics look good.
Maya Li: risks: false positives for normalization (we strip punctuation) could collide for heavily tokenized code prompts. add a whitelist to skip normalization for prompts classified as code-like.
Evan R: good catch. will add language/code heuristic (e.g., presence of triple backticks or code tokens) to skip exact drop and force flagging instead.
LabelBot: noted. job artifacts and counts available at s3://label-dryruns/dryrun-176119-2026-03-22.csv and cloudwatch logs group /prefilter/dryrun/176119
Omar Patel: thanks folks. after PR and one dry flip well run a canary on the int4 pool to confirm hallucination/truncation rates haven't worsened.
Maya Li: perfect. document decisions in the PR and ping #release-war-room when flipping the toggle. thanks everyone :rocket:
